findings.text: Incoming transport connection requests are admitted by selecting a local terminal, applying an allow-list check, and establishing at most one active association per terminal before enabling deferred output handling.
Each terminal toggles between disconnected and connected transport states, entering connected only through successful admission and returning toward disconnected handling on sever notification.
Terminal selection supports two modes: a wildcard request binds any currently disconnected terminal, while a named request binds only the terminal whose service identity matches.

Per-terminal exclusion guards inspection and mutation of connection state and association during admission, with wildcard scans briefly holding each candidate exclusion while testing disconnected status.
A global filter guard allows concurrent admission checks under shared access while exclusive access serializes replacement of the allow-list contents.
Data path queues and peer identity are guarded by per-terminal exclusion, with receive and completion paths using normal exclusion and status inspection using bottom-half safe exclusion.
Admission enforces uniqueness by discarding any extra request when the chosen terminal is already associated, and discards refused requesters after severing their proposed association.
Accepted associations request a maximum inbound message limit of 65535 and assemble a sixteen byte negotiation token from halves of the requester identity.

Inbound messages are rejected when oversized, when the local endpoint is still closed, or when short-term buffer allocation fails; otherwise their descriptors are queued for the service thread to consume.
Send completion matches outstanding descriptors by identifier, extracts the completed entry under exclusion, wakes output waiters, then releases storage after dropping exclusion.
Three read-only device attributes expose terminal identity with encoding translation, a numeric pair of transport and endpoint states, and the current peer identity when connected.
Device visibility groups three attributes into one group and terminates both the attribute list and the group list with null sentinels.
The IUCV personality plugs into the generic console core through operations for character transfer, endpoint lifecycle notifications, hangup, and modem control.

Terminal creation initializes synchronization, queues, deferred output work, waiters, staging storage, console marking, generic console binding with interrupt-driven notification, service naming, and device registration.
Creation failures unwind in reverse order of acquisition, and teardown removes generic console binding and device registration before releasing staging and private storage.

Allow-list text is a comma separated sequence of short blank-padded uppercased identities, rejecting empties, lone wildcards, overlong entries, and oversized lists, with empty input clearing the list.
A kernel parameter exposes the allow-list with gated access that requires virtualized execution and configured terminals, deferring early writes and rendering current entries as comma separated text.

Driver initialization validates environment and device count, applies any deferred allow-list, prepares buffer caching and pooling, instantiates the console before terminals, creates each terminal, then registers transport callbacks with full unwind on failure.
An early boot option parses a decimal terminal count, warns on malformed input, and always reports the option as consumed.

OPAL consoles distinguish raw and packet protocols per terminal, storing the selector plus packet state in a private record tracked in a fixed-size table with a dedicated early boot instance and terminal number.
Device tree binding claims serial nodes with compatible values ibm,opal-console-raw and ibm,opal-console-hvsi for the two supported modes.
Raw OPAL operation set binds character transfer and drain plus interrupt-driven lifecycle notifications to generic console callbacks.
Packet-mode OPAL helpers resolve per-terminal state by number, fail when absent, then delegate transfer to shared packet helpers or chain interrupt setup before packet open.
Shared packet helpers provide console-readable character input, bounded character output, and endpoint open with establishment for reuse by transport personalities.
Packet sessions handshake by clearing establishment and resetting sequence before exchanging version queries and responses, returning to unestablished on close requests.
Reception validates headers, waits for complete packets, exposes only data payloads to readers, and dispatches control and query traffic internally while compacting consumed bytes.
Transmission numbers every outbound packet with a monotonically increasing sequence and caps each data packet payload to the implementation maximum, propagating transport errors.
Carrier state tracks a dedicated modem bit and, on loss for non-console opened endpoints, initiates close to trigger higher layer hangup.
Packet sequencing relies on atomic counter operations rather than explicit exclusion, with reset during handshake and increment on every send.
Packet transfer guards against missing state with warnings and device errors, suppresses input before open, and reports broken pipe when unestablished.
Resource and configuration failures surface as out-of-memory, no-device, invalid-argument, or no-space errors with logging and cleanup that leaves no partially registered terminals.
Attribute encodings translate service identities between host and display character sets, append newlines, and render state as paired decimals and peer as paired identities separated by punctuation.
Packet validity requires a header byte at or above hexadecimal FC and at least four buffered bytes before length inspection, with data payloads starting after a four byte header.
Service identities are eight byte blank-padded tokens with fixed prefix lnxhvc plus numeric suffix, and a wildcard form using that prefix plus blanks selects any free terminal.
Admission schedules deferred output work after a short delay of five time units, staging uses one page, and generic console binding requests a 256 entry transfer area.
